edits: add F at ring position 3 of 2,5-dichloro-BQ
accepted.hypothesis: The closest result so far was a trihalo BQ with two Cl and one F (f 1.17, margin 0.157, bind -25.0). Moving Cl from 2,6 to 2,5 kept f near 1.10 and bind -25.3 with no detachment. That points to F added on a 2,5-Cl2 core as a promoted direction. One F should lift the margin above 0.15 and keep the one open C-H, which limits the binding loss seen with fully substituted rings (D14, D11). K020 reports strong dichloro-BQ binding and K084 shows F-BQ adducts. I avoided CN (all detached) and NH2/OH (lowered f). Reaching f>=2 is unlikely, but this tests whether the 2,5 geometry adds binding.

edits: add Br at ring position 5, leaving one C-H
accepted.hypothesis: The trihalo BQ with one open C-H (2,3-Cl2-5-F) was the best margin/f balance so far (0.157, 1.17). Replacing F with Br should raise the margin further (D11 Br4 had 0.462) and give some room above 0.15. Only one Br is used, since D11 shows that Br4 collapses binding (-19.2, f 0.28). This tests whether the margin can be gained with a heavier halogen while the open C-H keeps binding. It is a direction that raised the margin; Br is limited to one to avoid the f drop.

edits: replace F with Cl at ring position 5
accepted.hypothesis: D08 (F4) has margin 0.178 and f 1.03. D07 has a stronger bind (-25.8), but only 0.097 margin. A BQ with a 2,3-difluoro pair and one Cl on the opposite side, with two open C-H, mixes F-driven margin with Cl-driven binding. The open C-H sites reduce crowding at the carbonyls. Expected margin is about 0.15, bind about -25. This is a less halogenated step than the failed tetrahalo variants. The risk is that the margin falls just under 0.15.

edits: add F at positions 4 and 5 (bay region) of phenanthrenequinone
accepted.hypothesis: D15 has the strongest CO2 binding (-27.9, f 1.09) but a margin of -0.196. Distal F at 2,7, 3,6 and 1,8 and four F at 2,3,6,7 raised the margin only to between -0.05 and -0.12 while losing some f. A bay-region F at 4,5 is a different electronic position, conjugated through the biaryl bond, and it twists the biphenyl. That may shift the LUMO and the margin more than the earlier placements. The dione-adjacent positions 1,8 kept bind -27.3, so the o-quinone binding mode should hold. K117 reports a very large CO2 adduct constant for PQ. This is a lower-confidence exploration of the PQ core; it avoids CN, NH2 and OH.

edits: replace F with Cl at ring position 3
replace F with H at ring position 6
accepted.hypothesis: The closest result so far is the trihalo-BQ with one open C-H (2,3-dichloro-5-fluoro: f 1.17, margin 0.157). It kept the margin above 0.15 and lost less binding than the tetrahalo BQs (D14 f 0.72, D11 f 0.28). D07 (bind -25.8, f 1.24) and D08 (bind -24.3, no detachment) both support small halogens with an open C-H. I promote that direction and flip the halogen ratio to two F and one Cl on D08's frame. F is smaller than Cl, so it should cost less carbonyl-region crowding and keep the CO2 binding. The one Cl and two F should still lift the margin toward 0.15 or more, since D08 (F4) reached 0.178. This tests whether the F-rich trihalo pattern gets more binding than the Cl-rich one. I avoid CN (D03, D06, D10 detached CO2) and NH2/OH (D01, D02, D04, D05 lowered f), and I avoid Br and a full set of heavy halogens (D11). K084 and K020 report CO2 adducts for F4-BQ and a dichloro-BQ. Risk: f is unlikely to reach 2, since no reference has, so the best realistic outcome is f above 1.2 with a margin of at least 0.15.

edits: add F at ring positions 3 and 6 of 2,5-dichloro-BQ
rejected.hypothesis: D08 (F4) kept bind -24.3 and gained margin 0.178. Chlorines gave the stronger binding (D07 -25.8). A para-symmetric 2,5-Cl2-3,6-F2 BQ keeps a Cl/F balance without any Br, which hurt binding in D11. It should give a margin above 0.15, and the symmetric dipole may help CO2 binding. The risk is that it ends near f 1, like the other tetrahalo BQs (D08 1.03, D14 0.72). No CN, NH2 or OH.
